key_insight: Disordered carbon materials share glass-like thermal transport that is better described by two or three activated coherence channels with approximately recurring energy ratios.
engineering_relevance: The framework could improve temperature-dependent thermal conductivity models for porous and disordered carbon components across varied densities and microstructures.
method: Measure thermal conductivity from 4.5 to 300 K in GO, reduced GO, GO–hydrated fullerene, expanded graphite, and graphite–MWCNT composites.
Model transport using a Peierls contribution plus up to three Arrhenius-type coherence channels.
Compare activation energies and channel amplitudes across materials and with published disordered-carbon data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports failure of the single-coherence-channel model, recurring ratios E2 ≈ 4E1 and E3 ≈ 12–25E1, and amplitudes that increase with density while activation energies remain nearly invariant.
watch_item: The model is phenomenological; the abstract provides no quantitative fit uncertainties or direct microscopic validation of the proposed coherence channels.
paper_title: Universal Multichannel Coherence-Mediated Thermal Transport in Carbon Allotropes: Experimental Evidence and Scaling Laws
